newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Chemical fertiliser use cuts Bangladesh food yield.
newsitem.headline: Chemical fertiliser use cuts Bangladesh food yield.

text.p: A Bangladesh report said on Saturday that the country's food yield had been dwindling because of unplanned use of chemical fertiliser and toxic pesticides.
The report said the per hectare yield of rice fell to 3.5 tonnes now from five tonnes in 1970.

"Indiscriminate use of chemical fertiliser and toxic pesticides in agricultural land is lowering the country's food production, particularly the high yielding variety of rice," said the report prepared by a research institute and quoted by official BSS news agency.
It said research had found a disproportionate use of nitrogen, phosphorous and potassium in farmland, resulting in a lower crop yield.
"This has deteriorated the whole agricultural situation, creating hindrances to attaining food self sufficiency in the country by the year 2000," the report said.
Bangladesh produces about 19 million tonnes of rice and wheat annually for the country's nearly 120 million people. It imports up to two million tonnes to meet a shortfall.
